What `gh-inbox` writes into today's note:

```markdown
{{< meta facts.marker.inbox_start >}}
*updated at 2026-11-04 {{< meta facts.time.job >}} from {{< meta facts.ph.host >}}*

**Waiting on you**
- [ ] [Add retry to uploader](https://github.example.com/<your-org>/<team-repo>/pull/318) · `<your-org>/<team-repo>` · review requested · 3h ago
- [ ] [Flaky deploy step](https://github.example.com/<your-org>/<team-repo>/issues/97) · `<your-org>/<team-repo>` · mention · 2d ago

**Oldest**
- [ ] [Document the release flow](https://github.example.com/<your-user>/<personal-repo>/issues/12) · `<your-user>/<personal-repo>` · assigned · 41d ago

*14 more items hidden (17 total).*
{{< meta facts.marker.inbox_end >}}
```

- **{{< meta facts.inbox.waiting >}}**: review requests, mentions and direct replies from the last {{< meta facts.inbox.waiting_days >}} days, at most {{< meta facts.inbox.waiting_max >}}.
- **{{< meta facts.inbox.oldest >}}**: the {{< meta facts.inbox.oldest_max >}} stalest items, to close or bump. Optional.
- One line counts the items neither list shows.
- The `updated at` stamp is the heartbeat: missing or not today's means the job didn't run.
- If one source fails (for example, notifications), the block is still written, with a `> [!warning] Could not fetch …` line under the stamp, and `gh-inbox` exits 1 so the [launchd wrapper](launchd.qmd) alerts. If every source fails, the note is left unchanged and it exits 1.
- If today's note doesn't exist, `gh-inbox` exits with an error, doesn't create it, and makes no GitHub calls.
